scope: Ordinary Store insertion into existing spare capacity and suffix truncation; complete existing impl236 library target replay.

identity.algorithm: SHA256 of lexically sorted path + NUL + lowercase file SHA256 + LF
identity.paths: Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, tracked lib/**, crates/**/src/**, crate Cargo.toml; build.rs is separately bound below
identity.verification: Independently recomputed from exact Git blobs. The author manifest excludes build.rs; its exact Git hash is additionally recorded here. Std library source and ZIL fixtures are embedded in the harness.

retained_harness.binding: Copied before target reuse and independently hash-verified against the committed receipt.

runtime_input_binding: allocator_probe.c independently matched its exact Git SHA256 in both root and author worktrees before and after the replay.
source_review: insert validates 0 <= index <= length < existing capacity before changing the input. length-index is nonnegative and bounded by length. It allocates the complete fresh suffix before moving any original element; failure returns the actual incoming owner.

The private helper only receives distinct original/fresh suffix stores. First transfer moves exactly length-index elements into a reserved suffix. The original then has index elements and at least one spare slot for the incoming value; restoring the suffix requires at most original length+1 slots, already bounded by original capacity. Existing native push does not allocate; pop fails only when empty, excluded by the loop condition. Ignored helper/push errors are unreachable under these actual caller invariants.

Two reversals restore original suffix order. Each actual owning value is popped once and pushed once per transfer; no owner is duplicated or dropped during successful transfer. The temporary suffix ends empty and its allocation is freed.

truncate checks the requested range before mutation, then pops and drops actual last elements until the desired length. Capacity remains unchanged. Negative and excessive lengths leave the original store intact.
The two Rust changes are semantic-neutral: remove an unnecessary borrow and name an existing return tuple type. No compiler privilege is added for library names.

controls: empty/front/middle/append insertion and actual element order
suffix preparation failure preserves original values, length and capacity
invalid index and full capacity return and clean the actual incoming owner
negative/excessive/partial/zero truncation, reverse suffix destructor order
live allocation count zero after every execution
nearest source live Store view across insert rejects in Analyze or Verify before Build

limitations: The source live-view negative is a source-pipeline rejection, not a separate raw Analyze and Verify mutation pair.
insert deliberately requires existing spare input capacity and allocates a temporary suffix. No implicit input growth or performance parity is claimed.
Author Clippy not independently rerun; no full-workspace, native-Windows, Rust comparison, complete collection API or full-language acceptance.
